## Question 4 - Logistic Regression

# Load related Functions/Variables

Functions files are from Section 08 folder

```{r Setup}
library(MASS)
library(class)
library(ggplot2)

load("cancer_PC.RData")
load("BCWData_balanced.RData")

source("get.train.R")
source("example.display.R")
source("p.hat.R")
```

# Select Principal Components for 90% Variance

```{r PC_select, echo=FALSE}
cancer_pc_summary <- summary(cancer_PC)
cumulative_var <- cancer_pc_summary$importance[3, ]
num_PCs <- which(cumulative_var >= 0.90)[1]

cat("Number of PCs needed for 90% variance:", num_PCs, "\n")
```

Store into a dataset

```{r update data, echo=FALSE}
BCWData_pca_90perVar <- as.data.frame(predict(cancer_PC,BCWData_balanced)[, 1:num_PCs])

```

# Convert Class labels

2 = Benign -\> 0, 4 = Malignant -\> 1

```{r Class convert, echo=FALSE}
BCWData_pca_90perVar$Class <- ifelse(BCWData_balanced$Class == "2", 0, 1)

str(BCWData_pca_90perVar)
```

# Split Data to Training & Testing sets

Define `%w/o%` in "get.train().R". And the define function is from "without.R" in Section 8 folder.

```{r helper Define, echo=FALSE }
"%w/o%" <- function(x,y) x[!x %in% y]
```

In machine learning, a common split for a dataset is 80% for training and 20% for testing. In other words, the split_indices is adjustable.

```{r TrainTest Sets, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(123)  

split_indices <- get.train(nrow(BCWData_pca_90perVar), train.sz = round(0.8 * nrow(BCWData_pca_90perVar)))

train_data <- BCWData_pca_90perVar[split_indices$train, ] 
test_data <- BCWData_pca_90perVar[split_indices$test, ]   

train_data$Class <- as.factor(train_data$Class)
test_data$Class <- as.factor(test_data$Class)

cat("Training samples:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Test samples:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
```

# Logistic Regression Model

```{r LR Model, echo=FALSE}
log_model <- glm(Class ~ ., data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(log_model)
```

# Visualizing Logistic Regression

Find the best 2 PCs for Visualization (highest coeff)

```{r Visualization_SetUp, echo=FALSE}
coef_values <- abs(coef(log_model)[-1])  
best_pcs <- names(sort(coef_values, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2]  

train_pca_2D <- train_data[, c(best_pcs, "Class")]
train_pca_2D$Class <- as.factor(train_pca_2D$Class)

train_pca_2D_matrix <- as.matrix(train_pca_2D[, best_pcs])
```

Visualize using `example.display()`

```{r Visualization_p1, echo=FALSE}
model.exp <- expression(glm(Class ~ ., data = train_pca_2D, family = binomial(link = "logit")))
predict.exp <- expression((p.hat(model, points) > 0.5) * 1)

example.display(train_pca_2D_matrix, train_pca_2D$Class, {}, {},
                c(100, 100), paste("Logistic Regression (", best_pcs[1], " vs ", best_pcs[2], ")"),
                model.exp, predict.exp)
```

Visualize using `ggplot2`

```{r Visualization_p1, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(train_pca_2D, aes_string(x = best_pcs[1], y = best_pcs[2], color = "Class")) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3) +
  labs(title = paste("Logistic Regression -", best_pcs[1], "vs", best_pcs[2]),
       x = best_pcs[1], y = best_pcs[2], color = "Class") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Generate Predictions & Store for later Use

```{r predictions, echo=FALSE}
pred_probs <- predict(log_model, test_data, type = "response")
predictions <- ifelse(pred_probs > 0.5, 1, 0) 

predictions <- as.factor(predictions)
save(pred_probs, predictions, file = "logistic_predictions.RData")
```
